look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · UNARMED green black nightshade with ovate ALTERNATE leaves and WHITE flowers. Most distinctive: an apparently UNEVEN inflorescence (one branch with several flowers, another seeming to carry a single basal flower); anthers medium-length ~1.8–2.5 mm. DEVELOPING fruit has relatively long RECTANGULAR/OBLONG GREEN CALYX lobes with ROUNDED tips. Fully ripe berries commonly 10–14 mm wide and shiny BLACK. This is primarily a GREAT PLAINS species; a similar Hays County plant is not automatically S. interius. Confirm with reproductive detail or hold as Solanum morelloid complex.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted North American taxon with Texas records in GRIN and 2019 revision, most frequent Great Plains. No verified Hays County occurrence or county native scoring.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Encounter-based comparison species only; native-by-county audit paused.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Solanaceae: leaves alternate, flowers with joined usually 5-part corolla, 5 pollen-producing anthers, berry fruit. Unarmed morelloids distinguished from the larger prickly Solanum.
best_field_traits: Unarmed green herb or short-lived subwoody perennial to around 1 m; base branching; broad ovate, simple alternate leaves, margins entire or shallowly toothed.
White five-lobed star-shaped corolla; projecting yellow anthers roughly 1.8–2.5 mm long, longer than S. emulans (1.5–1.8 mm in 2019 revision).
UNEVEN-LOOKING inflorescence: a cluster of several flowers and a separate solitary-looking basal flower that is actually differently articulated on a pedicel.
Green calyx lobes relatively LONG, rectangular-to-oblong, apices rounded, particularly clear in developing fruit (photograph 3).
Berries generally mature to glossy purplish-black; around 10–14 mm in diameter (larger than emulans ~6–8 mm); black gloss alone not species-diagnostic.
Seeds typically ~1.8–2.0 mm; often only 2–4 hardened stone cells per ripe berry. Compare nigrescens 1.2–1.5 mm seeds and >6 stone cells.
Photos A–C are research field collections Nee 61350, and D is RBGE cultivated material; none is proof of a Hays County occurrence.
morphology_keys.habit: Branching green or slightly straw-colored herb, annual to somewhat persistent under trees; the 2019 revision emphasizes low-forest/shaded and open sand-hill habitats over the Great Plains. Leaf/plant height alone weakly diagnostic.
morphology_keys.leaves: Simple alternate green ovate-broadly ovate leaves, commonly about 4.5–11.2 × 2.3–6.8 cm in revision; wavy to shallowly toothed margins; hairs variable. Do not use leaf holes or pale shade as a species ID character.
morphology_keys.flower: White five-lobed rotate/stellate corollas with yellow anthers approximately 1.8–2.5 mm long. Watch UNEVEN cluster arrangement and the articulation of its solitary-looking basal pedicel (about one-quarter to one-third its length upward according to revision). A hand lens and metric scale are recommended.
morphology_keys.fruit: Round berries GREEN when immature then BLACK and approximately 10–14 mm at maturity. Calyx lobes are relatively long, rectangular, rounded-tipped; in mature fruit the green calyx persists under berry. Figure 22D depicts genuine mature black berries, whereas C is developing fruits. 2–4 sclerotic granules and larger seeds are advanced confirmatory characters.
morphology_keys.habitat: The 2019 monograph calls this primarily a Great Plains nightshade, in open sand hills and shaded low forest/under trees; Texas statewide documented, Hays County local applicability unresolved.
morphology_keys.management: Not a food-identification card. Do not eat berries or leaves; Morelloid nightshade taxonomy is difficult and plants can contain toxic alkaloids. When unsure, photograph flower/anthers, flowering-axis branching and mature fruit/green calyx together.

field_terms.anther: Yellow pollen-bearing organ. Measure length with 1 mm reference: S. interius ~1.8–2.5 mm, often longer than emulans but overlapping nigrescens.
field_terms.calyx: The green sepals directly under flower/berry, often five; interius has comparatively longer rectangular lobes with rounded tips.
field_terms.pedicel: Individual flower/fruit stalk. The basal flower's articulation point contributes to the distinctive uneven-looking inflorescence.
field_terms.inflorescence: Branching arrangement of a flower cluster, not just a single flower. An uneven branch bearing multiple flowers plus a solitary-appearing basal flower matters in interius.
field_terms.stone_cell: Hardened non-seed granule inside a berry. Typically 2–4 in interius versus >6 in nigrescens; for trained botanical analysis only.

crew_field_sequence: 1 · Confirm an UNARMED Solanum with alternate ovate leaves and little WHITE flowers; avoid premature species call.
2 · Photograph the FULL flower cluster from the side: does one branch carry several flowers while another appears to have one basal flower? Seek pedicel articulation.
3 · Macro flower with a metric ruler: measure YELLOW ANTHERS, about 1.8–2.5 mm in interius.
4 · Photograph DEVELOPING fruit head-on: identify LONG, somewhat RECTANGULAR, ROUNDED-tip green CALYX lobes.
5 · Seek MATURE fruit, scale beside berry: ~10–14 mm black shiny berries; check calyx at berry base.

6 · Compare: emulans has shorter anthers (~1.5–1.8 mm), smaller ~6–8 mm fruit, differently shaped calyx. Nigrescens overlaps anther size; use more regular flowers, seed/stone cell, provenance and expert review.
7 · In Hays County, absent clear evidence, label Solanum black-nightshade complex / compare rather than assigning Great Plains interius by glossy black fruit alone.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Main key is an UNEVEN inflorescence with distinctive basal pedicel, medium anthers, long rounded-tip calyx, larger black berries. Multiple structures, never one character alone.

field_matrix.calyx: Long rectangular lobes with ROUNDED tips
field_matrix.quick_rule: UNEVEN flower cluster + mid-sized anthers + long rounded calyx + larger black berries

field_matrix.flower: Usually less uneven cluster; anthers ~1.5–1.8 mm in 2019 revision
field_matrix.calyx: Appressed/spreading lobes not typically as rectangular-long and rounded-tip
field_matrix.seed_stone_cells: Seeds ~1.6–1.8 mm; stone cells often more
field_matrix.quick_rule: Shorter anthers and smaller fruit than interius; fruit calyx alone overlaps.

field_matrix.flower: Anthers overlap 1.8–2.5 mm; flowers more REGULARLY spaced and sometimes branch with more than one flower
field_matrix.berries: Generally smaller or similar dark berries
field_matrix.calyx: Calyx can also hug/spread under berry
field_matrix.seed_stone_cells: Seeds only ~1.2–1.5 mm and >6 stone cells
field_matrix.quick_rule: Anthers overlap: use arrangement and seed/stone cells, and consider range; don't guess.

field_matrix.flower: Tiny white stars; SHORT yellow anthers ~0.8–1.5 mm
field_matrix.calyx: Very SMALL lobes strongly REFLEXED away from ripe berry
field_matrix.quick_rule: Much shorter anthers + green calyx bent backward at fruit base.

field_matrix.berries: Dark fruit varies in size and sheen
field_matrix.quick_rule: Introduced complex; not separable from black berry photo alone.

not_reliable_alone: Only a glossy black berry: interius and americanum may both be glossy.
Only white five-part flowers: shared across numerous morelloids.
Only leaf shape or low stature: overlaps emulans and nigrescens.
Mature fruit size without a ruler or comparable scale: can mislead.
Inflorescence branching not well photographed: avoid confident species label.
Great Plains distribution is helpful background, NOT an independent morphological confirmation.

items.creator: Michael Nee
items.caption: Developing GREEN fruit with persistent green calyx, photographed before the berries turn black. Relatively long rectangular-to-oblong lobes have rounded tips; note the calyx lobes surround the berry. Don't mislabel them as petals or claim the green berry is ripe. Photo: Michael Nee in Knapp et al. (2019) Fig. 22C, CC BY 4.0. This is an attributed photo crop. Arrow correction from user's iPhone QA: the left calyx arrow lands directly on an elongated sepal blade, the right on the outer rounded lobe tip, and the lower pointer marks a visible green developing berry body instead of the calyx junction. These are developing, not ripe black berries.

items.label: LOOK-ALIKE — eastern black nightshade developing fruit
items.image_role: DIFFERENT species: developing fruit calyx of S. emulans
items.creator: Michael Nee
items.caption: THIS IS S. EMULANS, NOT S. INTERIUS. Both can have green calyces close to fruit, but S. interius typically has longer mid-size anthers, larger berries and more rectangular, rounded-tip calyx lobes.
items.why_it_matters: Avoid identifying by appressed calyx alone; this photograph is deliberately clearly labeled a DIFFERENT species.

items.label: LOOK-ALIKE — divine nightshade mature fruit
items.image_role: DIFFERENT species: small, dark berry with green calyx
items.creator: Jorge Manuel Valdez-Carrasco
items.caption: THIS IS S. NIGRESCENS, NOT S. INTERIUS. Both may have mid-sized anthers, and fruiting calyces close to the berry. Interius is more Great Plains-associated and differs in distinctive uneven clusters, longer rounded-tipped calyx lobes, larger seeds and fewer berry stone cells.
items.why_it_matters: A dark berry with an appressed calyx is NOT sufficient to declare interius.
